title: Abu Sufyan and Hind
hookLine: leaders of Mecca's opposition, who became Muslim when Mecca opened

lines: WHOEVER ENTERS HIS HOUSE IS SAFE.
cards: Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says it on the day Mecca opens, as Sahih Muslim records. A strange sentence, once you know whose house that was.
At the end of Uhud, it was Abu Sufyan, leading the Meccan army, who called across the field: is Muhammad among the people? Is Abu Bakr? Is Umar?
He cried out in praise of Hubal, the idol of Mecca, and the answer came back, as Sahih al-Bukhari records it: God is higher and more majestic. Now that same man's front door is named a refuge.
Today: Abu Sufyan, and his wife Hind.

teach.b: For years Abu Sufyan led Mecca's opposition to the Prophet. Hind, his wife, stood with him; the biographies tell hard stories of her at Uhud, around the death of the Prophet's uncle Hamzah.
Then came the opening of Mecca, the conquest, when the Muslims entered the city and the enemy's house became a shelter. Abu Sufyan, the biographies say, became Muslim. Then Hind.
Bukhari keeps her words, and they are startlingly honest.

teach.h: NO HOUSEHOLD I WANTED HUMBLED MORE.
teach.b: There was a time, she told the Prophet, when no household on the face of the earth was one I wanted humbled more than yours.

teach.h: NOW NONE I WANT HONORED MORE.
teach.b: Today, no household on the face of the earth is one I want honored more than yours. She didn't pretend the past away. She named it, then named the change.

The Prophet answered with an oath of his own, by the One in whose hand is his soul. In the same report she goes straight on to a household problem: Abu Sufyan is tight with money; may she take what her children need?
Yes, she's told, what is reasonable. From enemy of a house to ordinary questions within the community, in one conversation.
They came late, after years of fighting, after Uhud and all it cost. Sunni tradition counts them among the companions. The door was not shut because they arrived at the end.

how: Muslims remember the opening of Mecca as a day of amnesty, when former opponents, Abu Sufyan and Hind among them, were given safety and became Muslim.

o: a battle in which Mecca's walls were broken down
a peace treaty signed outside Mecca's gates
the opening of Mecca, when old enemies were given safety

games.q: Abu Sufyan and Hind — tap the pairs.
p: Abu Sufyan calls across the field
no household I want honored more
what she may take for her children

s: the Prophet named Abu Sufyan's house a place of safety
whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe, in Sahih Muslim.
Hind pretended she had never opposed the Prophet
she said it outright: no household I wanted humbled more, and now none I want honored more.
Abu Sufyan was a supporter of the Muslims at Uhud
he led the Meccan army and called out across the field after the battle.

games.q: you are Hind, coming to the Prophet after the opening of Mecca. what do you say about the past?
o: name it honestly, and name the change.
say you were forced into it.
games.why: she said no household on earth was one she wanted humbled more, and now none she wanted honored more. in Bukhari.

practice: Bring to mind someone you once opposed, a rival, an old classmate, a relative you clashed with, and try Hind's two sentences quietly.
Finish the first honestly, back then, I saw you as, and then the second, now, I see; if the second is hard to finish, that is worth knowing too. If you pray, you can pray for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Fath, the opening, the conquest of Mecca after which Abu Sufyan and Hind, once his fiercest opponents, became Muslim and were welcomed in. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: opening; the word used for the opening, or conquest, of Mecca.

carryVoice: Your line: late, and welcome. Coming at the end still counts as coming. See you tomorrow.
